messages:
olivia: quick heads-up — after onboarding q4-llama-int8 on the funccall pipeline we're seeing intermittent structured-output parse failures in the evaluator. failure rate ~0.7% overall but jumps to ~3% on prompts with long tool args. :thinking:
Samir: any consistent symptom? truncated JSON, bad quoting, or extra text? :eyes:
olivia: mostly malformed JSON — unescaped control chars, occasional trailing commas, and sometimes stray Unicode tokens like \u2581 sequences breaking parsers. happens more when kv-prefix cache is warm.
Jia: paste of a recent raw model output (copied from runner):
```
{"tool":"search","args": {"query": "best printers 2025",}, "request_id":"abc123"}
Some follow-up text: recommended models include the new X-Print 5.
```
Jia: notice the trailing comma after "query" and then extra free text appended. standard json.loads blows up.
bench-bot: automated smoke run 2026-02-14T09:01Z: funccall-eval v2 — 10k samples, pass (strict schema) 99.3%, pass (lenient rescue) 99.9% — regression relative to fp16 baseline: +0.6% failures on strict parse.
Marcus: two hypotheses: 1) int8 quant noise changes tokenization boundaries (▁ tokens) causing stray commas/quotes. 2) batching + kv cache occasionally mixes response prefixes leading to appended text.
Samir: good call. can we reproduce deterministically? try single-request, no-batching, kv-cache disabled, same prompt seed. if it disappears -> caching/batching bug. if persists -> tokenization/quant issue.
olivia: ran single-request with cache disabled — failure rate drops to 0.02%. looks like cache interaction increases risk.
Jia: example rescue strategy I prototyped: try json5 tolerant parse first, if that fails run a heuristic extractor that finds the first balanced {...} block, then try to canonicalize (remove trailing commas, fix unquoted keys). small snippet: 
```
import re, json
s = model_output
m = re.search(r"(\{.*\})", s, flags=re.S)
if m:
    candidate = m.group(1)
    candidate = re.sub(r",\s*\}", "}", candidate)
    parsed = json.loads(candidate)
```
This recovers ~70% of failures in smoke tests.
Samir: I hate heuristics but pragmatic. We should also add a hard fallback route: if strict parse fails and rescue succeeds, record as "rescued" and route more traffic to the non-quant fp16 for that prompt bucket while we fix runtime.
Marcus: ops suggestion: add a short circuit in the kvcache write path to avoid overlapping prefixes when batching boundary is ambiguous. we'll add an assert on prefix_len equality.
qa-bot: scheduled an AB test: next deployment will split 5% traffic to q4-llama-int8 with rescue postprocessor enabled and compare downstream tool correctness metrics for 48h. report job id: funccall-smoke-20260214-42.
olivia: plan of action: 1) enable rescue parser (json5 + extractor) in prod as metric-only for 24h, 2) run no-cache reproduce matrix across temps/top_p/beam 3) instrument kv-cache with per-request tags to detect cross-talk, 4) rollback policy: auto-failover to fp16 if rescued_fraction > 0.5% for a route.
Samir: also add literal-token-debug logging for cases where rescue triggers (dump token ids + detokenized with markers). helps check if quantization introduced weird token boundaries.
Jia: i'll push the rescue parser PR with tests and add a small regression harness that checks for trailing commas and stray-text. will add a unit that verifies we never silently drop tool calls.
Marcus: i'll take the kvcache assert + release a hotfix to staging by EOD.
olivia: thanks team. if someone sees a spike outside the AB, ping me immediately. :rocket:
